In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms that control the migration of the testis from the abdominal cavity into the scrotal position.
the role of the RLF gene in the development of the testicles and the scrotum in mammals.
the molecular and cellular events that control the development of the male reproductive system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
RLF is a critical factor for testicular descent, and that RLF acts on the gubernaculums of the rat during early phases of testicular descent.

the relaxin-like family peptide 3 (RLP3) is the only RLF receptor that can bind RLF and that it is present in the gubernaculus of male rats at a time when the gubernaculus is growing and the testes descend.
the gubernaculum growth and testicular descent is dependent on RLF and that the RLF receptor is expressed in the gubernaculus during the period when the testis is descending.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
RLF is a hormone with an important role in male sexual development.
RLF is a hormone that regulates the migration of the testis from its prenatal position in the abdomen to its final position in the scrotum.
the INSL3 gene is a critical factor in male reproductive development, and the INSL3 hormone is a critical factor for the development of the gubernaculum.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the synthetic ROLF is biologically active, which is important for future studies.
the RLF receptor is present in the gubernaculus and that the receptor is not up-regulated as the testis migrates.
